title: Regions and grooves fast, and off the first-paint path: the region build and SurfaceCreases are each a small fraction of today's ~2 s on a crawfish scan, and the scene paints before they finish
description:
User 2026-10-25: since TOOL-49 the ring scene builds its regions (1.7 s on IMG_4112, 938k faces) whichever tool is active, and the ring tool measures the grooves (SurfaceCreases.of, 2.0 s) when the graph has no surface_creases node, both before the first frame; the user expected regions only on Ctrl+T. Also IxdarWindow prints 'Time to First Paint' before the render loop starts, so it is not the first frame.
1. The first frame draws the surface as soon as the graph has a surface: region build and groove measurement run after it, off the render thread or spread across frames, and their results swap in when ready (regions colour in, labels appear).
2. TOOL-49's rule stays true: the regions dataset is current whenever read (an automation read waits for the build or reports it is building, it never returns stale data).
3. 'Time to First Paint' is measured at the first frame actually presented.
Evidence: references/load-times-2026-10-25.md in the tickets repo.

SCOPE (user, 2026-10-25): moving the work after first paint is only part of it; the region build (1.7 s on IMG_4112, 938k faces, 299 regions) and the groove measurement (SurfaceCreases.of, 2.0 s, mostly computeEdgeDihedrals) should not take seconds at all. Profile both on IMG_4111/IMG_4112 (warm and first run) and make them fast: one pass over edges for the dihedrals with primitive arrays (no per-edge objects), smoothing as a fixed number of sparse passes, parallel over faces/edges where independent; for regions, a single union-find/flood over faces using the rings' edges (with CRAW-86's per-ring edge lists if it has landed, else coordinate), no repeated whole-mesh clears, flatness from the same pass. Share the dihedral step with the cross field's feature-edge test (CrossField.featureDihedralCos) if it can be one computation. Results identical (region rows, flatness values, crease strengths, ring fingerprints).
definition-of-done:
1. Region build and groove measurement each under 200 ms on IMG_4111 and IMG_4112 on this machine (warm), first run reported; before/after table.
2. The first frame is presented before they finish (log timestamps); Time to First Paint measures the first presented frame.
3. Results identical (region rows, flatness, crease strengths, fingerprints); ui-state regions never stale (test).

Keeps RegionsAndCreasesBenchmark's [bench] lines: the explicitly run benchmark's timings and result digests are its output, the before/after and identity evidence.

The benchmark's kept lines are '[bench] ring' (ring fingerprints), '[bench] creases #' (groove timings and checksums) and '[bench] regions #' (region timings and digests).
testing-plan:
1. mvn test.
2. Live: launch the ring scene on IMG_4112, read the log timestamps.
changes-made: SurfaceCreases.of builds its curvature from flat arrays (fan triangles, triangle normals, 1-rings) in parallel passes instead of computeEdgeDihedrals' HashMaps; PrincipalDirectionField.oneRings(triangles) orders each 1-ring exactly as the old edge map iterated it (spread-hash order, falling back to the map when ids outgrow its table), so crease strengths are bit-identical; smoothing and edge costs run as parallel sparse passes; quantiles by quickselect. CrossField.featureDihedralCos is a polygon-face normal dot test, not this computation, so nothing is shared.

RingRegions: face tables, areas and centroids built in parallel; ring masks read with a vectorised Arrays.mismatch scan in parallel per ring; per-slot wall flags for the floods; nearestActiveFace reads cached centroids in parallel (MeshLabels.resolve 300 ms to 14 ms). RegionExplosion.measure and HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.uploadFacePickBuffer compute per-face terms in parallel and keep their sums in face order. Results identical (benchmark digests, ring fingerprints, saved .dsl).

RegionLayer builds a new surface's regions on the frame after it is first drawn; building() says when regions are not current, ui-state reports regions.building and no rows meanwhile, builtRingRevision is set only after labels resolve. IxdarWindow prints 'Time to First Paint' after the first presented frame (GLFW swap / headless first paint). New RegionsAndCreasesBenchmark, PrincipalDirectionRingOrderTest and a RegionControlAutomationTest case for the building state.

Synced onto master d76fb8e4 (25 commits). Conflicts: launch.json kept master's Trade Game entries and the CRAW-87: ring-tool entry; State.java uses master's toastRows() helper and drops absorbSlivers (removed by CRAW-89), keeping regions.building; HalfEdgeMeshRuntime keeps master's shading constants plus PICK_FACES_PER_TASK; RegionLayer keeps master's resolvedPalette/colouredByPart and palette-swap branch beside drawnSurface/building(), the palette re-resolve now runs only when the regions are current; automation_routes.json regenerated by mvn compile. RegionsAndCreasesBenchmark adapted to rebuild() without the absorb threshold and to Palettes.DARK.region/categories (UI-17). mvn test 781 run, 0 failures; wt done passed.

Synced onto master 9f263e75 (2026-11-07). Master's MESH-91/MESH-92 had replaced the helpers this ticket rewrote and accepted the result changes, so the reference is now master's output, not the 2026-11-04 one. Resolutions: SurfaceCreases uses mesh.signedVolume(); RingRegions keeps its parallel per-face pass with mesh.faceArea(); computeEdgeDihedrals keeps triangleNormals() plus master's TriangleSoup.edgeFaces(); EdgeDihedrals.vertexNormals delegates to a new static SemanticPatchDecomposer.vertexNormals(triangles, faceNormals, bound), which PrincipalDirectionField now uses; State reports regions.building with master's regionLookPicked() for visible. PrincipalDirectionField's HashMap-order oneRings emulation (and HASH_MAP_* constants, MIN_BARYCENTRIC_AREA, PrincipalDirectionRingOrderTest) is gone: master builds rings with TriangleSoup.oneRings, so this ticket does too.
TriangleSoup.oneRings rebuilt on flat arrays in parallel, giving exactly the order of the HashSet<Integer> it replaces (first table 8, doubling past 3/4, bucket order, insertion order within a bucket; a vertex whose bucket reaches 7 entries is read off a real set). It was 220-270 ms of the 300 ms the groove measurement still took after the sync; crest, saddle, Morse-Smale, MSC cell and boundary-snap callers get the same rings faster. New TriangleSoupRingOrderTest compares it against the HashSet version on 40 generated soups (ids spread to share buckets, ids above 2^16, degenerate triangles, a 150-blade fan). Verify tests: TriangleSoupRingOrderTest, RegionControlAutomationTest.
Before/after (RegionsAndCreasesBenchmark body run against master's build and this worktree's, alternating, 8 repetitions, load 4-7, ms): IMG_4111 creases 1962 first / 1608-1848 warm -> 136 first / 84-122 warm; regions 1012 / 190-478 -> 369 / 120-364 (settles 120-125); labels 582 / 542-674 -> 68 / 17-21. IMG_4112 creases 1820 / 1560-2019 -> 113 / 95-176; regions 643 / 151-697 -> 347 / 110-225 (settles 110-118); labels 356 / 388-594 -> 71 / 10-12. Ring, crease (strength, curvature, cost, saturation) and region (all 17 digests) results identical to master on both scans.
Live ring-tool scene, IMG_4111 (load ~9): master surface_creases 2509 ms, regions logged at 10.4 s; this branch surface_creases 560 ms, first frame presented 7.3 s, regions 8.3 s. IMG_4114 (no rings, grooves measured by the tool): master ready 4.3 s, grooves 2810 ms, regions 8.1 s; this branch first frame 4.8 s, grooves 651 ms, regions 6.2 s. repair_mesh (~1.9 s cold) is now the largest single stage.
mvn test from the reactor root: 820 run, 1 error, PatchColoursTest.scalarShaderHoldsTheRampPalette, which fails on master too (VIEW-31 deleted glsl/mesh_scalar.fs, the test still reads it). wt done passed: build, 19 named tests, launch entry, screenshot tmp/craw-87-launch.png.
review-summary: SurfaceCreases and RingRegions now build from flat arrays in parallel passes, and RegionLayer builds a new surface's regions only after its first frame is shown. Loading a crawfish scan spent about four seconds on grooves and regions before anything appeared.
